newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen flat-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs sold steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, with prices underpinned by light marketings, livestock dealers said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $55.50 to $56.50 in the country and up to $58.00 for hogs delivered to plants, they said.

Illinois hogs sold fully steady to $0.50 higher at $56.50 to $57.50 in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants, although several packers were willing to pay $1.00 premiums for top quality hogs. Indiana hogs sold steady at $56.00 to $56.50 in the country and $58.00 to $58.50 at plants.
Ohio hogs sold steady in light trading at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $57.00 to $58.00 at plants, dealers said.
Hog marketings were light on a seasonal basis, and held back further by active fieldwork as farmers finish planting soybeans and attend to rapid weed growth, they said.
Weeds have been prolific, especially in the eastern belt, because of the wet, cool spring, sources there said.
Cash hog price gains were tempered by light demand from packers struggling with unprofitable operating margins. Lower pork prices on Tuesday pushed margins deeper into the red, the dealers said.
